# Module `lune_ui_core::ui`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

The per-window `Ui` frame: stable widget ids under scopes, a retained store with transient and
keep-alive state, layered hit testing with pointer capture, [`Response`](ui.md#struct.Response), animated values, the
overlay stack with modal capture, dismissal and exit retention, focus scopes, key routing,
semantic nodes with accessibility actions, strings, and the [`FrameOutput`](input.md#struct.FrameOutput) (with [`Repaint`](input.md#enum.Repaint))
a frame returns.

A frame: [`Ui::begin`](ui.md#method.Ui.begin) resolves this frame's events against the previous frame's hit regions,
overlays, tab stops and semantic tree (D4), widgets call [`Ui::interact`](ui.md#method.Ui.interact) and draw through
[`Ui::painter`](ui.md#method.Ui.painter), and [`Ui::finish`](ui.md#method.Ui.finish) closes the overlays the app stopped calling (drawing their
exit frames), turns this frame's regions into the next frame's, drops unused state and returns
the `Scene` and the `FrameOutput`. Hits from `interact` and from raw `Painter::hit` calls share
one ordered list, so widgets of both APIs mix in one frame; `painter.hover` is the hovered id
(D3).

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/ui.rs:1`

**Methods and associated items**

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.drag_dim"></a>`pub fn drag_dim(&mut self, id: WidgetId, dragged: bool) -> f32`

  The opacity of a source card: [`DIM_ALPHA`](drag.md#constant.DIM_ALPHA) while it is the one being dragged, else 1, with
  the `selection` transition.

- <a id="method.Ui.drag_gesture"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn drag_gesture(
      &mut self,
      id: WidgetId,
      resp: &Response,
      drag: &mut ReorderDrag,
      strip: &Strip<'_>,
  ) -> DragFrame
  ```

  Feeds `drag` from item `id`'s `resp` (`Sense::DRAG`): call it for every item every frame, and
  before [`Self::drag_offset`](ui.md#method.Ui.drag_offset) so the offsets are this frame's. A primary press on an item arms
  the machine (this item then owns the gesture; other items' calls only report `dragging`);
  while it is held the pointer feeds `update` and `tick`; a release reports
  [`DropResult`](drag.md#enum.DropResult). The gesture cancels on Escape (taken only while dragging), when the
  item count of `strip.metrics` changes, and when the capture ends without a release. While the
  auto-scroll delta is non-zero the frame asks for another. The owner's node, if already
  emitted, gets `State::Pressed` while armed or dragging.

  The app applies a `Commit` to its order, and applies `scroll_by` to the strip's scroll
  offset.

- <a id="method.Ui.drag_offset"></a>`pub fn drag_offset(&mut self, id: WidgetId, drag: &ReorderDrag, index: usize, x: f32) -> f32`

  The horizontal offset to draw item `index` (id `id`, unshifted layout position `x` in strip
  content coordinates) with while `drag` runs, and for the settle after its release; 0
  otherwise. The dragged item follows the pointer with no transition; every other item slides
  to its slot (`move`); after a release the released item settles (`settle`). Both are
  animations of the item's absolute position keyed by `id`, so applying a `Commit` to the
  layout changes nothing the animation sees. Call it for every item every frame, after
  [`Self::drag_gesture`](ui.md#method.Ui.drag_gesture).

- <a id="method.Ui.free_drag_gesture"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn free_drag_gesture(
      &mut self,
      id: WidgetId,
      resp: &Response,
      drag: &mut FreeDrag,
      source: u64,
      columns: &[Column<'_>],
  ) -> FreeFrame
  ```

  [`Self::drag_gesture`](ui.md#method.Ui.drag_gesture) for a [`FreeDrag`](drag.md#struct.FreeDrag): item `id` carries `source`; `columns` are in
  window coordinates. Escape, a change of the column count and a capture that ends without a
  release cancel it. A press and its release inside one frame are a [`FreeResult::Click`](drag.md#variant.FreeResult.Click).

  The gesture only sees an item that still calls it: when `source` leaves the items, the
  caller cancels `drag` itself, or it stays live with nobody to end it.

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.node"></a>`pub fn node(&mut self, node: Node)`

  Appends `node` to the frame's tree: its parent is the open container, its bounds go
  through the transform stack, and the Ui owns its `focused` state. Ignores the node's own
  `parent` and `children`. Inside a disabled scope ([`Ui::with_enabled`](ui.md#method.Ui.with_enabled)) the node is
  `Disabled`, not `Focusable`, and offers no action, whatever it asked for.

- <a id="method.Ui.node_container"></a>`pub fn node_container<R>(&mut self, node: Node, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Appends `node` and makes it the parent of the nodes `f` emits.

- <a id="method.Ui.previous_tree"></a>`pub fn previous_tree(&self) -> &SemanticTree`

  The previous frame's semantic tree.

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.animate_color"></a>`pub fn animate_color(&mut self, id: WidgetId, target: Rgba, motion: &Motion) -> Rgba`

  [`Self::animate_f32`](ui.md#method.Ui.animate_f32) for a colour, channel by channel (straight alpha); exactly `target`
  once settled. In the frame the theme changes it snaps to `target`, whether `target` moved
  or not: a theme swap is a hard cut (D5), so no colour fades from the old theme to the new.

- <a id="method.Ui.animate_f32"></a>`pub fn animate_f32(&mut self, id: WidgetId, target: f32, motion: &Motion) -> f32`

  `target` animated per `motion`: the first call for `id` returns `target` and is not in
  flight; a changed target retargets (keeping position and velocity, D11), or snaps when the
  motion resolves to nothing in this tier. While the value moves the frame asks for
  `Repaint::Now`.

- <a id="method.Ui.snap_f32"></a>`pub fn snap_f32(&mut self, id: WidgetId, v: f32) -> f32`

  Settles the transition of `id` at `v` and returns `v`: a later [`Self::animate_f32`](ui.md#method.Ui.animate_f32) with
  target `v` is not in flight, one with a new target starts from `v`.

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.request_focus"></a>`pub fn request_focus(&mut self, id: WidgetId)`

  Focuses `id` at the next frame's begin, without the ring.

- <a id="method.Ui.rove_focus"></a>`pub fn rove_focus(&mut self, id: WidgetId)`

- <a id="method.Ui.rove_keys"></a>`pub fn rove_keys(&mut self, items: &[(WidgetId, bool)], axis: RoveAxis, wrap: bool) -> Option<usize>`

  Moves focus inside a roving composite: while a child is focused, takes the arrows of `axis`,
  Home and End (not a Control, Alt or Command chord, which stays a shortcut), skips disabled
  children, calls [`Self::rove_focus`](ui.md#method.Ui.rove_focus) on the new child and returns its index. A key that
  finds no move is still taken. Call it every frame: the Tab order reads the list it was
  given.

- <a id="method.Ui.rove_stop"></a>`pub fn rove_stop(&self, items: &[(WidgetId, bool)], active: Option<usize>) -> Option<usize>`

  The child of a roving composite that is its tab stop this frame, given its `(id, enabled)`
  children in order: the focused enabled child, else `active` if enabled, else the first
  enabled, else none. Register that child as a stop and the others with [`Sense::CLICK_ROVE`](ui.md#associatedconstant.Sense.CLICK_ROVE).

- <a id="method.Ui.set_composing"></a>`pub fn set_composing(&mut self, id: WidgetId, composing: bool)`

  Says whether `id` is composing text (an open IME preedit). While the focused widget
  composes, the next frames' Escape and Tab are not handled by the frame: they join the focus
  event queue instead. Cleared when focus moves off `id`.

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.consume_focus_event"></a>`pub fn consume_focus_event(&mut self, index: usize)`

  Takes the event at `index` of [`Self::focus_events`](ui.md#method.Ui.focus_events); the frame then asks for a catch-up
  frame. An index out of range or already taken does nothing.

- <a id="method.Ui.consume_key"></a>`pub fn consume_key(&mut self, id: WidgetId, key: NamedKey) -> bool`

  Takes this frame's next press of `key` for `id`: true once per press, when `id` is the
  focused widget of the active scope (or the target of a synthetic key). A consumed real key
  turns the focus ring on.

- <a id="method.Ui.consume_key_while_pressed"></a>`pub fn consume_key_while_pressed(&mut self, id: WidgetId, key: NamedKey) -> bool`

  Like [`Self::consume_key`](ui.md#method.Ui.consume_key), but for the widget that holds the pointer capture, whatever the
  focus (a drag that Escape cancels). A key counts when `id` holds the capture now, or held it
  where the key arrived in the frame's events: an Escape that came before the release of the
  same frame is the gesture's, though the release has ended the press by the time the
  widget asks.

- <a id="method.Ui.focus_events"></a>`pub fn focus_events(&self, id: WidgetId) -> Vec<(usize, FocusEvent)>`

  The frame's unconsumed input for `id`, in arrival order, each with the index
  [`Self::consume_focus_event`](ui.md#method.Ui.consume_focus_event) takes it by: keys (named and character, with modifiers and
  the repeat flag), typed text, IME events and clipboard answers. Empty unless `id` holds the
  key focus of the active scope (or is the target of a synthetic key).

- <a id="method.Ui.code_editor"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn code_editor(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      doc: &mut CodeDoc,
      opts: &CodeOptions<'_>,
  ) -> CodeResponse
  ```

  A code view under `key` over `rect` on `doc`: lines of mono text with a gutter, read-only or
  editable as `opts` says. Only the lines in view are built, so its frame costs the same at
  any line count.

  Editable, it behaves as [`Self::text_area`](ui.md#method.Ui.text_area) without the box: keys, typed text, clipboard
  answers and IME events edit `doc`, and the caret comes into view at once. Read-only, it is
  a Tab stop with no caret: a press focuses and selects, Select all and Copy work, the Page
  keys, Home and End scroll, and the arrows stay free for a binding.

- <a id="method.Ui.code_line_rect"></a>`pub fn code_line_rect(&mut self, key: impl Hash, line: usize) -> Option<Rect>`

  The rect of line `line` (from 1, as the gutter numbers it) of the view under `key`, in the
  space the view was drawn in, as the last call left it: as wide as the view, for an overlay
  pinned to the line ([`ANCHOR_INSET`](widgets/code_editor.md#constant.ANCHOR_INSET) from the right edge). `None` out of view or out of
  range, so an overlay that is not there registers nothing.

- <a id="method.Ui.scroll_area"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn scroll_area<R>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      opts: &ScrollOptions,
      content: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &ScrollView) -> (R, Extent),
  ) -> ScrollResponse<R>
  ```

  A scroll area under `key` over `rect`. `content` draws in content coordinates (the area
  translates it by the negative offset, clipped to `rect`) and returns its value and its
  [`Extent`](widgets/scroll_area.md#struct.Extent); with [`ScrollOptions::extent`](widgets/scroll_area.md#structfield.ScrollOptions.extent) given, the returned extent is ignored.

- <a id="method.Ui.scroll_area_untranslated"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn scroll_area_untranslated<R>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      opts: &ScrollOptions,
      content: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &ScrollView) -> (R, Extent),
  ) -> ScrollResponse<R>
  ```

  [`Self::scroll_area`](ui.md#method.Ui.scroll_area) without the translation: the content places itself from
  [`ScrollView::offset`](widgets/scroll_area.md#structfield.ScrollView.offset) (a virtual list subtracts in `f64` and casts the small result, which
  an `f32` translation could not do at a million rows). The clip, the input, the thumb and the
  node are the same. A keyboard focus move to a child that shows only in part brings it into
  view by the least movement, as in a translated area; a child placed over the whole viewport
  (a list's own region) has nothing to reveal, and a scroll-into-view stays the content's
  business.

- <a id="method.Ui.scroll_to"></a>`pub fn scroll_to(&mut self, key: impl Hash, target: Target, how: Reveal)`

  Asks the scroll area under `key` (of the current scope) to bring `target`, a box in its
  content coordinates, into view. Applied when the area is next called (this frame if it
  comes later, or from inside its content). A target outside the content changes nothing.

  Made after the area in the frame, it asks for the frame that applies it, unless the target
  already shows, so an app may call this every frame and still settle to `Repaint::Idle`.


  A spinner under `key`, the glyph centred on `center`. Turns while `opts.busy` under Full
  (asking for the next frame); a static glyph at angle 0 under Reduced and Off. The node is
  `Progress` named `opts.name`, `Busy` while busy, with no value.

`impl Ui<'_>`

- <a id="method.Ui.split_panes"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn split_panes(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      opts: &SplitOptions<'_>,
      draw: impl FnMut(&mut Ui<'_>, Pane, Rect),
  ) -> SplitResponse
  ```

  A split under `key` in `rect`. `draw` is called for each pane with its rect, `First` then
  `Second`, clipped to that rect and under a scope of its own; the strip is drawn and
  registered after both. The sized pane is hidden when `opts.hidden`: only the other is drawn,
  on the whole rect.

  The panes are drawn with the size the frame ends with: the pointer's and the keys' size is
  worked out before they draw. An accessibility set-value is read with the strip's own
  region, after the panes, so it shows in the panes on the catch-up frame it asks for.

- <a id="method.Ui.split_state"></a>`pub fn split_state(&mut self, key: impl Hash) -> &mut SplitState`

  The persistent state of the split under `key`, in the current scope: the sized pane's
  stored size, for the app to load and to store. It lives while a split is drawn under `key`
  (also hidden) or a keep-alive scope around the last one is.

- <a id="method.Ui.tab_strip"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn tab_strip(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      tabs: &[Tab<'_>],
      opts: &TabStripOptions<'_>,
  ) -> TabStripResponse
  ```

  A tab strip under `key` over `rect` (normally [`HEIGHT`](widgets/tab_strip.md#constant.HEIGHT) high, at the top of `opts.card`),
  with the new-tab button after the last tab, or at the right end when the tabs overflow.
  The strip is only as wide as its tabs, so a press in the space after them reaches whatever
  is under the strip. A closable tab reserves its close column, so a hover or an activation
  moves no tab; a change of `opts.active` slides the outline's notch to the new tab ([`SLIDE`](widgets/tab_strip.md#constant.SLIDE)).
  Call it every frame. Read `events` and apply them to the app's list; the strip never
  changes it. A secondary click (or the show-menu action) on a tab comes back as `context`,
  the tab and its rect; the strip opens no menu, the app opens its own with [`Ui::menu`](ui.md#method.Ui.menu)
  there. See the module docs.

  ```rust
      rect: Rect,

      cell: impl FnMut(&mut Self, &CellCtx) -> Cell,
  ) -> TableResponse
  ```

  A table under `key` over `rect`: the header on top, the rows under it in a scrolling body.
  `row_key` names the row at an index; `cell` is called for each cell of each row in view and
  either answers the text the table draws or draws a widget of its own in the cell's rect
  and answers [`Cell::Control`](widgets/table.md#variant.Cell.Control). Widgets in a cell have their ids under the cell's scope.

- <a id="method.Ui.table_selection"></a>`pub fn table_selection(&mut self, key: impl Hash) -> &mut ListState`

  The retained selection of the table under `key` (of the current scope): the body list's,
  see [`Ui::list_state`](ui.md#method.Ui.list_state).

- <a id="method.Ui.table_state"></a>`pub fn table_state(&mut self, key: impl Hash) -> &mut TableState`

  The retained sort of the table under `key` (of the current scope). The app may change it.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.outside_modals"></a>`pub fn outside_modals<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Runs `f` on [`LayerId::Outside`](scene.md#variant.LayerId.Outside), a surface that stays live and undimmed under a modal: a
  modal's dim, blur and input block do not reach what `f` draws and registers, at any modal
  depth. `f` draws under the current clip and transform; the painter's layer, clip,
  transforms and hit tag come back afterwards. An overlay opened inside `f` that asks for
  `Popup` or `Modal` is on `Outside` too, above `f`'s own drawing by tag; one that asks for
  `Toast` stays there. Keys are unchanged: Tab stays trapped in the modal and Escape goes to it.

  The switch is not recorded, so it does not replay: the scope belongs at an app's top level,
  not inside [`Self::record`](ui.md#method.Ui.record).

- <a id="method.Ui.overlay"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn overlay<R>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl std::hash::Hash,
      options: &OverlayOptions,
      exit: impl Fn(&mut Painter<'_, WidgetId>, f32, bool) + 'static,
      content: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'a>, &OverlayFrame) -> R,
  ) -> (OverlayFrame, R)
  ```

  Draws the overlay `key` this frame: pushes it on the stack when it is not open (or reopens
  it from where its close got to), runs `content` on `options.layer` with its hits tagged to
  the overlay and its own focus scope, and keeps `exit` to draw its closing frames once the
  app stops calling it. `exit` gets the linear close progress and `transforms`.

  A `Popup` or `Modal` overlay opened above an active modal draws on [`LayerId::Raised`](scene.md#variant.LayerId.Raised)
  instead, or on [`LayerId::Outside`](scene.md#variant.LayerId.Outside) when a modal under it is on `Outside` (a dialog opened
  from [`Self::outside_modals`](ui.md#method.Ui.outside_modals)), so it is above every modal either way. That is settled at
  open or reopen. On each later frame the same rule runs again over the older modals still on
  the stack (open, opening, or closing with their exit not yet over), whatever later frames
  pass as `layer`, and the overlay takes the result when it is lower: it drops from `Outside`
  to `Raised` once the last `Outside` modal under it has finished its exit, and to the layer
  it asks for once no older modal is left (a dialog that replaces another in one frame is
  raised only during the first one's exit). It never rises mid-life. An overlay called inside
  the scope stays on `Outside` for the scope's sake, with or without a modal; a child that was
  on `Outside` because its parent was drops with the parent, in the same frame.
  Once closing, an overlay keeps the layer it has, so it exits where it drew. A reopen under
  a modal that opened during the close is an open above that modal. What `content` draws is
  the overlay's alone: a surrounding [`Self::record`](ui.md#method.Ui.record) does not get it.

- <a id="method.Ui.record"></a>`pub fn record<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> (R, Ops)`

  Runs `f` and returns what it drew as owned painter calls, for an exit painter to replay.
  Nests: inside another `record` the outer recording also gets what `f` drew. An overlay
  opened in `f` is not part of it: it exits through its own painter.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.begin"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn begin(
      store: &'a mut UiStore,
      input: &'a RawInput,
      config: FrameConfig<'a>,

  ```

  Starts a frame: resolves `input`'s events against the previous frame's hit regions,
  overlays, tab stops and semantic tree.

- <a id="method.Ui.clipboard_read"></a>`pub fn clipboard_read(&mut self)`

  Asks for the clipboard's text; the answer arrives as an event on a later frame. Repeated
  calls in a frame send one request.

- <a id="method.Ui.clipboard_write"></a>`pub fn clipboard_write(&mut self, text: String)`

  Puts `text` on the clipboard; the last write of a frame is the one sent.

- <a id="method.Ui.end_keep_alive"></a>`pub fn end_keep_alive(&mut self, key: impl std::hash::Hash)`

  Ends the keep-alive scope `key`: state kept only by it is dropped at this frame's finish
  unless used this frame.

- <a id="method.Ui.finish"></a>`pub fn finish(self) -> (Scene, FrameOutput)`

  Ends the frame: closes the overlays the app did not call and draws their exit frames,
  turns this frame's hit regions into the next frame's and drops unused state.

- <a id="method.Ui.id"></a>`pub fn id(&self, key: impl std::hash::Hash) -> WidgetId`

  The id of `key` under the current scope.

- <a id="method.Ui.input"></a>`pub fn input(&self) -> &'a RawInput`

  The frame's raw input (for events a widget handles itself, such as clipboard replies).

- <a id="method.Ui.interact"></a>`pub fn interact(&mut self, id: WidgetId, rect: Rect, sense: Sense) -> Response`

  Registers `rect` as a hit region of `id` on the painter's current layer and returns the
  frame's reading of it. The region is clipped and transformed like `Painter::hit`.

- <a id="method.Ui.keep_alive"></a>`pub fn keep_alive<R>(&mut self, key: impl std::hash::Hash, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Opens the keep-alive scope `key` (if it is not open) and runs `f` inside it, with ids
  nested under it. The scope stays live across frames, drawn or not, until
  [`Self::end_keep_alive`](ui.md#method.Ui.end_keep_alive); persistent state used inside survives while it is live (D6).

- <a id="method.Ui.keymap"></a>`pub fn keymap(&self) -> Keymap`

  The platform's keyboard conventions for this frame.

- <a id="method.Ui.mark_alive"></a>`pub fn mark_alive(&mut self, key: impl std::hash::Hash)`

  Opens the keep-alive scope `key` without drawing inside it.

- <a id="method.Ui.painter"></a>`pub fn painter(&mut self) -> &mut Painter<'a, WidgetId>`

  The painter this frame draws with; old-API widgets take it directly.

- <a id="method.Ui.persistent"></a>`pub fn persistent<T: Default + 'static>(&mut self, id: WidgetId) -> &mut T`

  State of type `T` for `id` that also survives undrawn frames while a keep-alive scope open
  around its last use is live.

- <a id="method.Ui.pointer_in"></a>`pub fn pointer_in(&self, rect: Rect) -> bool`

  Whether the pointer is inside `rect`, given in the current drawing space (it goes through
  the clip and the transform stack, as a hit region does), with nothing drawn above the
  current painter context over it: a higher layer, or the same layer and a later overlay (the
  order [`Self::finish`](ui.md#method.Ui.finish) picks a press target by, so `Outside` is above every modal). Ignores `enabled` and `Sense`, so
  it reads true over a disabled anchor, and reads the previous frame's regions.

- <a id="method.Ui.pointer_pos"></a>`pub fn pointer_pos(&self) -> Option<(f32, f32)>`

  The pointer's position in logical pixels, or `None` when it is outside the window.

- <a id="method.Ui.request_repaint_at"></a>`pub fn request_repaint_at(&mut self, t: Time)`

  Asks for a frame at app time `t`; the earliest request later than now wins. A request at
  or before the frame's time is due already and is ignored (it never hides a later one).

- <a id="method.Ui.scope"></a>`pub fn scope<R>(&mut self, key: impl std::hash::Hash, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Runs `f` with ids nested under `key`.

- <a id="method.Ui.scope_id"></a>`pub fn scope_id(&self) -> WidgetId`

  The id scope the current call runs under: what `Scope::Within` names.

- <a id="method.Ui.set_cursor"></a>`pub fn set_cursor(&mut self, icon: CursorIcon)`

  The cursor icon this frame asks for; the last call wins. Default: [`CursorIcon::Default`](input.md#variant.CursorIcon.Default).

- <a id="method.Ui.set_ime_area"></a>`pub fn set_ime_area(&mut self, area: Option<Rect>)`

  Where text is being edited this frame, in logical pixels, or `None` (the adapter then
  disables IME); the last call wins.

- <a id="method.Ui.tab_scope"></a>`pub fn tab_scope<R>(&mut self, order: i32, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Runs `f`; the regions it registers with [`Self::interact`](ui.md#method.Ui.interact) carry the Tab order `order`
  (0 outside any scope; a nested scope replaces the outer one). Tab visits the stops of a
  scope (an overlay's own, or the page's) in ascending order, and in registration order
  among stops of one order, so a host can draw its panes in the order it needs and still
  Tab through them in the order the user reads them. Roving groups and modal traps are
  unchanged: an overlay's stops are its own, whatever their order.

- <a id="method.Ui.theme"></a>`pub fn theme(&self) -> &Theme`

  The theme this frame draws with.

- <a id="method.Ui.tier"></a>`pub fn tier(&self) -> MotionTier`

  How much motion this frame plays (see [`MotionTier`](motion.md#enum.MotionTier)).

- <a id="method.Ui.time"></a>`pub fn time(&self) -> Time`

  The app's time for this frame.

- <a id="method.Ui.tr"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn tr<'k>(
      &self,
      key: &'k str,
  ) -> &'k str
  where
      'a: 'k,
  ```

  The text for `key`: the string table's, else the toolkit default, else the key. Borrows
  the table and the key, not the frame.

- <a id="method.Ui.tr_fmt"></a>`pub fn tr_fmt(&self, key: &str, args: &[&dyn Display]) -> String`

  [`Self::tr`](ui.md#method.Ui.tr) with the placeholders filled from `args` through the frame's `ArgFormat`.

- <a id="method.Ui.transient"></a>`pub fn transient<T: Default + 'static>(&mut self, id: WidgetId) -> &mut T`

  State of type `T` for `id`, dropped at the finish of the first frame that does not use it.

- <a id="method.Ui.with_enabled"></a>`pub fn with_enabled<R>(&mut self, enabled: bool, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R`

  Runs `f` enabled or not. Disabled, every `interact` inside still registers (and blocks) but
  reports nothing, and the painter draws at opacity 0.4.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.command_palette"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn command_palette(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      query: &mut String,
      palette: &Palette<'_>,
      glass: &DialogGlass,
  ) -> PaletteResponse
  ```

  The command palette under `key`; call it every frame it is open. `query` is the search
  text (edited in place); `palette` holds the rows the app found for it. Stop calling to
  close: the card then plays the dialog's close motion from what it last drew.

  Focus opens in the search box and stays there: Up and Down move the selection (wrapping,
  over rows and "show more" rows alike), Enter activates it, a click activates a row, and
  Escape or a click on the scrim reports `dismissed`. Tab never leaves the card. A
  destructive row reports its activation as any other: the app asks to confirm (a dialog it
  opens meanwhile draws above the palette and takes the keys).

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.dialog"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn dialog(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      dialog: &Dialog<'_>,
      glass: &DialogGlass,
      body: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'a>, f32, f32, f32),
  ) -> DialogResponse
  ```

  A modal dialog under `key`; call it every frame it is open. `body` draws the app's part
  (content x, y just below the message, content width) and gets the `Ui`, so it can hold
  widgets; it is drawn live and recorded, and a closing dialog replays the recording. Stop
  calling to close: the Ui then draws the close motion from retained state (180 ms Full,
  120 ms Reduced, none Off).

  Cancel is the first tab stop, Confirm the second and the initially focused one (D20), so
  Enter confirms at open. Escape, Cancel, a scrim click and an assistive technology's
  dismiss report `cancelled`; a click on the card does nothing. Overlays the body opens
  (a popover, a menu, a tooltip, a dropdown, a nested dialog) draw and take input above it.

- <a id="method.Ui.dialog_with"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn dialog_with(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      dialog: &Dialog<'_>,
      options: &DialogOptions,
      glass: &DialogGlass,
      body: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'a>, f32, f32, f32),
  ) -> DialogResponse
  ```

  [`Self::dialog`](ui.md#method.Ui.dialog) with `options`: the form width, the blurred scrim, a disabled confirm.

  A disabled confirm draws as the button's own disabled look and keeps its place; Enter,
  Space, a click and the default action do nothing, and the keys are consumed so no shortcut
  sees them. The open focus goes to Cancel, or nowhere when there is none.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.dropdown"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn dropdown<S: AsRef<str>>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      anchor: Rect,
      anchor_id: WidgetId,
      options: &[(S, bool)],
      selected: usize,
  ) -> DropdownResponse
  ```

  The options list of the combo `anchor_id` (at `anchor`, in window coordinates, as
  [`Response::rect`](ui.md#structfield.Response.rect) is), on the popup layer: non-modal,
  Escape and a press outside dismiss it (`dismissed`), focus returns to `anchor_id` when it
  closes. Up and Down move a keyboard highlight over the enabled rows (starting at
  `selected`), Enter or a click on an enabled row picks it (`picked`); a disabled row has no
  hit region. It opens and closes at once: call it every frame it is open.

- <a id="method.Ui.dropdown_with"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn dropdown_with<S: AsRef<str>>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      anchor: Rect,
      anchor_id: WidgetId,
      options: &[(S, bool)],
      selected: usize,
      opts: &DropdownOptions,
  ) -> DropdownResponse
  ```

  [`Self::dropdown`](ui.md#method.Ui.dropdown) with the row cap `opts` asks for. A list longer
  than `max_rows` scrolls (the wheel, the thumb and the keys): it opens with the selected row
  in view, and a key that moves the highlight brings that row into view.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.flyout"></a>`pub fn flyout(&mut self, key: impl Hash, f: &Flyout<'_>) -> FlyoutResponse`

  The flyout `f` on the popup layer, a glass popover: Escape, a press outside it and focus
  loss dismiss it (`dismissed`), and a click on a row, or Enter or Space on the lit one,
  picks it (`picked`). The rows are the menu's: Up, Down, Home and End move one highlight
  over the enabled rows, which are one tab stop. Opens and closes with the menu's curves:
  call it every frame it is open.

- <a id="method.Ui.flyout_window"></a>`pub fn flyout_window(&mut self, key: impl Hash, f: &Flyout<'_>) -> FlyoutResponse`

  The flyout `f` in a window of its own: the window is [`flyout_size`](widgets/flyout.md#fn.flyout_size) big and the card is
  its whole rect (the tray's flyout, D17). `f.anchor`, `side` and `align` are not used: the
  app placed the window ([`place_surface`](tray.md#fn.place_surface)). Everything else is
  [`Self::flyout`](ui.md#method.Ui.flyout), through the same popover, so the keys, Escape, focus loss, the motion and
  the exit are the ones tested there; the app hides the window once `dismissed` and the frame
  is idle.

- <a id="method.Ui.flyout_window_in"></a>`pub fn flyout_window_in(&mut self, key: impl Hash, area: Rect, f: &Flyout<'_>) -> FlyoutResponse`

  [`Self::flyout_window`](ui.md#method.Ui.flyout_window) in `area`, a rect of the window in window coordinates: the card's
  corner is the area's corner. A page that hosts a tray surface in a pane of its own window
  passes the pane. Placement is in window coordinates, as every overlay's is: an `Xform` does
  not move it.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.menu"></a>`pub fn menu(&mut self, key: impl Hash, rows: &[MenuRow<'_>], at: (f32, f32)) -> MenuResponse`

  A glass menu of `rows` at `at` on the popup layer: [`Self::menu_with`](ui.md#method.Ui.menu_with) with no anchor and
  the default name.

- <a id="method.Ui.menu_window"></a>`pub fn menu_window(&mut self, key: impl Hash, rows: &[MenuRow<'_>]) -> MenuResponse`

  A glass menu of `rows` that fills the window: the window is [`menu_size`](widgets/menu.md#fn.menu_size) big and the
  panel is its whole rect (the tray's menu, in a window of its own, D17). It is
  [`Ui::popover`](ui.md#method.Ui.popover) with the window as the rect, so the keys, Escape, the motion and the exit
  are the popover's, and focus loss dismisses it as well as an outside press: the app hides
  the window once `dismissed` and the frame is idle.

- <a id="method.Ui.menu_window_in"></a>`pub fn menu_window_in(&mut self, key: impl Hash, area: Rect, rows: &[MenuRow<'_>]) -> MenuResponse`

  [`Self::menu_window`](ui.md#method.Ui.menu_window) in `area`, a rect of the window in window coordinates: the panel's
  corner is the area's corner. Placement is in window coordinates, as every overlay's is: an
  `Xform` does not move it.

- <a id="method.Ui.menu_with"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn menu_with(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rows: &[MenuRow<'_>],
      options: &MenuOptions<'_>,
  ) -> MenuResponse
  ```

  A glass menu of `rows` on the popup layer, placed as `options` says, non-modal: Escape and
  a press outside dismiss it (`dismissed`), and that press reaches nothing, so a press on the
  trigger closes without reopening. A click on an item, or Enter or Space on the lit item
  (else the focused one), picks it (`picked`); Up, Down, Home and End move the highlight over
  the enabled items. Call it every frame it is open; stop calling to close it, and it fades
  out through its exit painter. The look follows D7: opening at progress `p` is
  [`menu_open_anim`](widgets/menu.md#fn.menu_open_anim)`(p)`, open is `menu_open_anim(1.0)`, closing at `p` is
  [`menu_close_anim`](widgets/menu.md#fn.menu_close_anim)`(p)`.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.popover"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn popover<R>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      options: &PopoverOptions,
      content: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'a>, Rect) -> R,
  ) -> (OverlayFrame, Placement, R)
  ```

  A popover on the popup layer: not modal; Escape, a press outside it (which reaches
  nothing) and focus loss dismiss it (`OverlayFrame::dismissed`), and focus returns to
  `anchor_id` when it closes. `content` draws inside the placed rect, after the surface. Call
  it every frame it is open; stop calling to close it: it fades out through an exit painter
  replaying what `content` last drew. Opens and closes with the menu's curves.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.search_picker"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn search_picker<S: AsRef<str>>(
      &mut self,
      key: impl Hash,
      rect: Rect,
      items: &[S],
      selected: &mut Option<usize>,
      opts: &PickerOptions<'_>,
  ) -> PickerResponse
  ```

  A search picker under `key` in `rect` over `items`. A click, Enter or Space on the trigger,
  or an accessibility default, expand or collapse action opens or closes the popup; opening
  clears the search and focuses the box. In the box, Enter picks the first match and closes;
  with no match it does nothing. A click on a row picks it and closes. Escape, a press
  outside, focus loss and disabling close. A pick writes `selected`, an index into `items`.
  Every close gives focus back to the trigger, unless focus went to another widget. A
  `selected` out of range reads as none, and is left as it is.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.toast_history"></a>`pub fn toast_history(&mut self, key: impl Hash, rect: Rect, toasts: &mut Toasts) -> f32`

  The notification history in `rect`: the header with its clear-all button, and the archived
  toasts newest first in a scrolling list. Returns the height it uses (`rect.h`). The list
  is a `List` of `ListItem` rows named by their messages; clear-all is a button.

- <a id="method.Ui.toasts"></a>`pub fn toasts(&mut self, key: impl Hash, toasts: &mut Toasts) -> ToastResponse`

  Draws `toasts` on the toast layer: the stack at the window's bottom right, newest at the
  bottom. Applies the frame's timers from `ui.time()`, asks for a frame at the next deadline,
  and animates arrivals, removals and expansion. Draws on the toast layer wherever it is
  called, outside any overlay and focus scope, and does not take part in a surrounding
  [`Ui::record`](ui.md#method.Ui.record).

  Reports the action button or Cancel pressed this frame. Dismiss and the body press act on
  the model themselves. A toast is a `Status` node (`Alert` for an error) named by its
  message and described by its detail; its default action toggles the log, `Dismiss`
  dismisses it. Buttons are tab stops of the scope below; nothing takes focus on its own.

`impl<'a> Ui<'a>`

- <a id="method.Ui.hover_dwell"></a>`pub fn hover_dwell(&mut self, id: WidgetId, active: bool, delay: Duration) -> bool`

  Whether `active` has held for `delay` (app time), counting from the frame it turned true.
  Transient state under `id`: it resets on a frame with `active` false and is dropped when
  not called. While pending it asks for a frame at the due time (`Repaint::At`).

- <a id="method.Ui.tooltip"></a>`pub fn tooltip(&mut self, anchor: &Response, text: &str)`

  A tooltip with `text` for `anchor`, below it (flipped and shifted to stay in the window).
  Call it after the anchor's own widget, every frame: it shows after the theme's tooltip
  delay of the pointer over the anchor (disabled ones too) or of keyboard focus on it, and
  is hidden the frame the pointer leaves; a press on the anchor or Escape hides it until the
  pointer leaves. Sets the anchor node's description to `text` (and its name when empty).

- <a id="method.Ui.tooltip_with"></a>

  ```rust
  pub fn tooltip_with(
      &mut self,
      anchor: &Response,
      size: (f32, f32),
      content: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'a>, Rect),
  )
  ```

  [`Self::tooltip`](ui.md#method.Ui.tooltip) with content of `size` (before padding) drawn by `content` into the rect
  it is given; the panel adds the padding and is at most 320 wide.

<a id="struct.WidgetId"></a>
### Struct `WidgetId`

```rust
pub struct WidgetId(/* private */);
```

A widget's stable identity across frames: a hash of its parent's id and its own key, so the
same path of keys gives the same id every frame. The hasher has fixed keys, so the value is
the same in every process.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/ui/id.rs:8`

**Methods and associated items**

`impl WidgetId`

- <a id="associatedconstant.WidgetId.ROOT"></a>`const ROOT: WidgetId = _;`

  The id of the window's root; every top-level widget is a child of it.

- <a id="method.WidgetId.from_value"></a>`pub fn from_value(raw: u64) -> WidgetId`

  The id whose [`value`](ui.md#method.WidgetId.value) is `raw`, for an adapter mapping an id back from an
  outside system. Nothing checks that a widget has it: a target the frame cannot find is
  ignored.

- <a id="method.WidgetId.value"></a>`pub fn value(self) -> u64`

  The raw hash, for logs and tests.

- <a id="method.WidgetId.with"></a>`pub fn with(self, key: impl Hash) -> WidgetId`

  The id of a child of `self` with `key`.
